replies.text: {"verdicts":[{"id":"T1","keep":true,"reason":"Design states any website can trigger pre-filled payment deep link; concrete attacker-payee confirmation fraud."},{"id":"T2","keep":true,"reason":"Attacker-controlled payee/amount reaching backend; distinct server-side trust/validation attack."},{"id":"T3","keep":true,"reason":"Custom scheme registration is in design; distinct spoofing attack by malicious app harvesting credentials."},{"id":"T4","keep":true,"reason":"Design says deep link opens confirmation screen pre-filled; no step-up auth; distinct local/device-access attack."},{"id":"T5","keep":true,"reason":"Website-triggerable link enables repeated forced screen opens; distinct availability harm."},{"id":"T6","keep":true,"reason":"Design names externally triggered payment confirmation; missing origin record blocks dispute resolution — specific, not generic."},{"id":"T7","keep":true,"reason":"Overlay/tapjacking on the genuine pre-filled confirm control is a distinct attack vector and fix."}]}
